2326dcec7e.q: How can someone realistically build muscle and lose fat simultaneously, according to Case Specific Nutrition sports dietitians?
2326dcec7e.a: You cannot build muscle and lose fat at the same time effectively. Instead, bodybuilders and athletes prioritize one goal: commit to a bulk phase to build muscle as fast as possible while minimizing fat accumulation, then cut to lose body fat while preserving muscle. The key is periodizing your nutrition—eating in a caloric surplus to fuel muscle growth, then in a deficit to lose fat—rather than attempting both simultaneously, which leaves people stuck in limbo.

2326dcec7e.rq: Muscle takes a very, very, very, very, very long time to develop, but fat comes just quick, just like that.

e91a820ce3.q: What is a Certified Specialist in Sports Dietetics (CSSD) credential and what expertise does it represent?
e91a820ce3.a: A CSSD is a sports dietitian credential that signifies focus on working with athletes and managing diet and exercise for chronic disease—weight loss, diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol. Sports dietitians have additional training in the intersection of nutrition and exercise, background in eating disorders and disordered eating in athletes, and approach nutrition from a fitness lens rather than nutrition alone.

27afbe12e8.q: What is the clinical Venn diagram concept in sports dietetics and how does it guide referrals between practitioners?
27afbe12e8.a: The clinical Venn diagram describes overlapping expertise between dietitians, personal trainers, and therapists. Dietitians should know nutrition primarily but understand exercise basics and refer to trainers for movement patterns and progressive overload. Trainers discuss nutrition basics but refer to dietitians when needed. Therapists address emotional eating but coordinate with dietitians. Each practitioner knows their edges and clinical scope while playing in the sandbox of overlap.

83dbeb06ea.q: Why do beginners mistakenly believe they can build muscle and lose fat simultaneously when they start exercising?
83dbeb06ea.a: Beginners experience an initial three to five pound muscle spike when starting exercise, which creates the illusion of simultaneous muscle gain and fat loss. However, this spike consists mostly of water retention in muscle, inflammation, and glycogen storage—not actual muscle hyperplasia. When beginners maintain a caloric deficit instead of eating to support muscle growth, the muscle becomes progressively inflamed, halting both muscle building and fat loss, leaving them stuck making no progress.
